title: Poisoning Agentic Alpha: Adversarial Vulnerabilities Across Roles and Architectures in Multi-Agent Trading Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.24069v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent trading systems, in which specialized agents collaborate through structured communication to produce trading decisions, are moving rapidly from research prototypes to live deployments that control real assets. The same inter-agent communication that makes them effective also exposes them: a corrupted signal can propagate to the final decision and translate into realized financial loss. Unlike prior attacks that presume privileged access to system internals, we restrict the adversary to what is practically reachable---the source data and prompts agents consume---yielding a low-barrier, and thus democratized threat model instantiated as role-specific adversaries.   We present the first systematic empirical study in the financial domain to characterize how an adversarial signal enters a multi-agent trading system and how far it survives toward the decision. translated_title: 毒化代理Alpha：多代理交易系统中跨角色与架构的对抗性漏洞
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24069v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：基于LLM的多代理交易系统，其中专门代理通过结构化通信协作产生交易决策，正迅速从研究原型转向控制真实资产的实际部署。使它们有效的代理间通信同时也暴露了它们：一个被破坏的信号可以传播到最终决策，并转化为实际财务损失。与先前假设对系统内部具有特权访问的攻击不同，我们将对手限制在实际可达到的范围内——代理消费的源数据和提示——从而产生一个低门槛、因此民主化的威胁模型，实例化为角色特定对手。我们提出了金融领域首个系统性实证研究，以描述对抗性信号如何进入多代理交易系统，以及它在向决策传播过程中能存活多远。沿角色轴，我们分解了一个广泛使用的交易管道。
tldr: 本研究首次系统性地揭示了LLM多代理交易系统中，仅通过操纵源数据和提示即可实现低门槛的对抗性攻击，且该攻击能跨角色和架构传播至最终交易决策，造成实际财务损失。
en_tdlr: This study is the first to systematically reveal that low-barrier adversarial attacks, achieved by merely manipulating source data and prompts, can propagate across roles and architectures to final trading decisions in LLM-based multi-agent systems, causing realized financial losses.
